note: One row per test. Details of a finding are published once it is fixed and released; until then only its severity is shown. Severities, from worst: critical (keys reachable without your approval), high, medium, low, info.

entries.title: Red team: relay and wire protocol
entries.scope: Relay API: request signing and replay windows, phone and machine authorisation, pairing, machine channel, delayed approvals, the near flag, push registration, rate and abuse limits, payment webhook.
entries.method: Code review against the protocol, then an attack harness run against a local copy of the deployed relay build; read-only checks against the test deployment.
entries.held: Replayed and expired calls, another phone's key, channel isolation, early release of delayed approvals, forged near headers, push registration for another phone, storage limits, unsigned payment webhooks.

entries.title: Red team: command line tool and core library
entries.scope: Agent escape, the daemon socket, leaks to logs and errors, output masking, reply and plan binding, the number match, all parsers.
entries.method: Code review and proof-of-concept attacks in throwaway homes; 12 fuzz targets for 10 minutes each with AddressSanitizer: about 49 million inputs, no crashes, hangs or memory errors.
entries.held: Other local users, values in logs and crash output, replies reused for another request, lowered levels, changed plans, early release by the relay, number-match guessing.

entries.title: Red team: Android app
entries.scope: Exported components and links, backups, Keystore and biometric binding, requests crafted by a hostile paired machine, notifications, logs and screenshots.
entries.method: Review of all app code and the shared Rust core, manifests of the release and debug builds, dynamic tests on an emulator.
entries.held: Level downgrade by a machine, approval without a strong biometric, new fingerprints, backups and device transfer, exported entry points, lock-screen content.

entries.title: Automated code review of the command line tool
entries.scope: The full command line tool before its merge to the main branch.
entries.method: GitHub Copilot code review, now required on every pull request in every public repository.
entries.extra: Also 5 correctness issues without security impact.

entries.title: Supply chain: relay and website
entries.scope: All 308 npm packages in both lockfiles, install scripts, the served QR code library, CI actions, deploy credentials.
entries.method: Registry signatures and provenance for every package, osv-scanner (including the OpenSSF list of malicious packages), npm audit, lockfile integrity, a byte comparison of the served script with the published package.
entries.held: No malicious, hijacked or look-alike package; every signature and provenance check passed; the served QR library is byte-identical to the published one.
entries.fixed: Install scripts off; new versions must be 7 days old; CI tools pinned in the lockfile; GitHub Actions pinned to commits; CI added to the website.

continuous: GitHub Copilot reviews every pull request; the main branch of every public repository accepts changes only through reviewed pull requests.
Fuzzing of every parser on each pull request (2 minutes per target) and nightly (1 hour per target).
cargo deny on every pull request: known advisories, licences, crate sources.
npm audit signatures in CI: registry signatures and provenance of every package.
Dependabot alerts and updates, with a 7-day minimum release age.
Secret scanning with push protection on every repository.
Shared protocol test vectors checked byte for byte by the core library, the relay and both apps.
Power-cut tests: unsealing is cut at every step and must resume without losing anything.
